title: 2 Michelin Star Restaurants: All {{n2}} in the World ({{guideYear}})

h1: All {{n2}} Two-Michelin-Star Restaurants in the World
summary: Every two-star restaurant, country by country, with chefs, tasting menu prices and the cheapest ways in.
keywords: how many 2 michelin star restaurants are there in the world
body:
There are {{n2}} two-Michelin-star restaurants in the world, according to the {{guideYear}} MICHELIN Guide editions, spread across {{n2Countries}} countries and territories. {{top2Country}} has the most, with {{top2N}}. Two stars means excellent, inspired cooking: in the Guide’s classic phrase, “worth a detour.” This list was last checked {{checked}}.

Below is every 2 Michelin star restaurant, country by country, with its chef, its cuisine and what the main dinner tasting menu costs. Each name opens the restaurant’s prices on The Starred Bill, each city our full price list for that destination, and each arrow the restaurant’s page on the MICHELIN Guide. The level above has its own list: every three-Michelin-star restaurant in the world.

How many 2 Michelin star restaurants are there in the world?

{{n2}}, in {{n2Countries}} countries and territories. That is about one in every {{oneIn2}} Michelin-starred restaurants, and more than three times as many as hold three stars ({{n3}}). The count moves after every guide’s ceremony, as restaurants are promoted, drop a star or close: the latest new and lost two stars are listed below the tables.

Which country has the most two-Michelin-star restaurants?

{{top2Country}}, with {{top2N}}, followed by {{second2Country}} with {{second2N}}, {{third2Country}} with {{third2N}} and {{fourth2Country}} with {{fourth2N}}. By city, Tokyo leads with {{n2_tokyo}}, ahead of Paris ({{n2_paris}}) and Kyoto ({{n2_kyoto}}). Most of France’s two-star tables are outside Paris, in small towns and country hotels, where the old “worth a detour” wording still fits best. For every country’s one-, two- and three-star counts side by side, see Michelin stars by country and state.

What does two Michelin stars mean?

Two stars is the MICHELIN Guide’s middle level, for cooking that is “refined and inspired”: dishes where the chef’s personality and the kitchen’s skill clearly come through. For decades the Guide summed it up as “excellent cooking, worth a detour,” between one star (“a very good restaurant in its category”) and three (“exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey”). Stars rate only the food on the plate, judged by anonymous inspectors who pay for their meals; the dining room, the service and the wine list don’t count toward them. More on how the levels work in What is a Michelin star?

Is two Michelin stars better than one?

Yes, in the Guide’s own terms: the levels are cumulative, so a two-star kitchen is judged to do everything a one-star kitchen does, with more personality and polish. In practice a two Michelin star restaurant usually means a longer tasting menu, a bigger team and a higher bill: the typical two-star dinner menu costs {{price2}}, against {{price1}} at one star and {{price3}} at three. Many diners find two stars the sweet spot, with cooking close to the top level at a little over half the price. A restaurant being considered for a second star gets repeated visits from inspectors first, as how restaurants get a Michelin star explains.

2 Michelin star restaurants in London

London has {{n2London}} two-star restaurants and the UK {{n2UK}}, all in the MICHELIN Guide Great Britain & Ireland. London menus are priced before a service charge, usually 12.5–15%, which is added to the bill. See our page of Michelin star restaurants in London for every starred restaurant in the city, with lunch and wine prices.

{{table:two-star-london}}

2 Michelin star restaurants in Bangkok

Bangkok has {{n2_bangkok}} two-star restaurants among its {{in_bangkok}} starred restaurants, and every 2 Michelin star Bangkok restaurant is in the Thailand table above. Many Bangkok menus are quoted “++”, meaning a 10% service charge and 7% VAT come on top of the listed price. Our Bangkok page has every starred restaurant in the city with its prices.

2 Michelin star restaurants in Tuscany

Tuscany has {{n2_tuscany}}, all of them in the countryside or on the coast rather than in Florence: Il Piccolo Principe in Viareggio, Campo del Drago near Montalcino, Caino in Montemerano and Arnolfo in Colle di Val d’Elsa. We cover them, with their wine and how to reach each from Florence or Siena, in 2 Michelin star restaurants in Tuscany.

New and lost two-star restaurants

Each guide updates its stars once a year, so this list changes after every ceremony. In each guide’s latest edition, {{gained2}} restaurants reached two stars ({{new2}} straight in at two and {{up2}} promoted from one), {{down2}} came down from three, and {{lost2}} lost their two stars, by closing or dropping to one.

{{table:two-star-changes}}

How much does a two-Michelin-star meal cost?

The typical two-star dinner tasting menu costs {{price2}} per person before drinks and service, with most between {{range2}}. Where a two-star restaurant serves a set lunch, it typically costs {{lunch2}}, and a wine pairing adds about {{wine2}} at dinner. The cheapest two-star dinner tasting menu we track is at {{cheapest2}} in {{cheapest2Place}}, at {{cheapest2Price}}. What the whole bill comes to, with service and tax in each country, is in How much does a Michelin star restaurant cost?
